concepts.title: Unity in Diversity: Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat
concepts.definition: Bharat is presented as a land of many languages, festivals and art forms held together by one bond; the Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat programme lets children meet friends from every state and see the unity inside the diversity.
concepts.key_idea: Many cultures and traditions live side by side, and knowing each other's art makes the nation one.
question_patterns: what is the ek bharat shreshtha bharat programme about
why is india called a land of unity in diversity
what has bharat been known for since ancient times
which geographical features of bharat does the passage mention
why do travellers find india attractive
what advice does the passage give to the people of india

solution_steps.action: recall what the main character does
solution_steps.explain: Retell the central events in one or two sentences, naming the main character.

solution_steps.action: trace the turn in the story
solution_steps.explain: Point out the moment where the character changes or learns something.
Say what the story teaches about life in one clear sentence.

concepts.title: Traditional Art Forms: Aipan, Dhokra and Kondapalli
concepts.section: Kalakritiyon ka Bharat, Let us read II
concepts.definition: Each state shows a craft: Aipan of Uttarakhand draws rice-flour designs on geru walls, Dhokra of Odisha casts brass figures through a wax mould, Kerala shapes coconut shells, and Andhra's Kondapalli toys are carved from soft hill wood.
concepts.key_idea: Folk arts carry the culture of a place; materials and steps of each craft grow from local life and nature.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr105.txt, Kalakritiyon ka Bharat, Let us read II
question_patterns: describe the aipan folk art of uttarakhand
how is a dhokra metal figure made step by step
what things are made from coconut shell craft in kerala
which wood is used for kondapalli toys and why
match each child with the state and the art form presented
why is coconut shell craft called biodegradable

solution_steps.explain: Note the state, the maker and the material of every art form.
Trace the order from raw material to finished piece for one craft.
Say what is common, such as natural materials and skill passed down.

concepts.title: Order Words in Craft Process Writing
concepts.section: Kalakritiyon ka Bharat, Let us learn
concepts.definition: Process writing uses order words such as to begin, first, then, after that, next and finally to fix the steps of a craft, so the reader can repeat the making exactly.
concepts.formula: process = first step + then steps + finally last step
concepts.key_idea: Order words turn a list of actions into a clear sequence anyone can follow.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr105.txt, Kalakritiyon ka Bharat, Let us learn
question_patterns: which words show the order of steps in a process description

why do we use words like first then and finally in process writing

what is the final step in making kondapalli toys

solution_steps.explain: Underline to begin, first, then, next and finally in the passage.

solution_steps.action: tie each word to a step
solution_steps.explain: Match every order word with the craft action it introduces.
Repeat the whole craft using the order words as signposts.

concepts.title: Ila Sachani: Embroidering Dreams with her Feet
concepts.definition: Ila Sachani, born without the use of her hands, learns to stitch with her feet and rises from a village girl into a nationally admired embroidery artist, showing that will can beat physical limits.
concepts.key_idea: A disability does not end ability; patience and family support turn Ila's feet into her hands.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr105.txt, Ila Sachani, Let us read
question_patterns: how did ila sachani learn to embroider with her feet
what difficulty was ila sachani born with
who encouraged ila in her early attempts
how did ila's work become known outside her village
what does the story of ila sachani teach us
which awards or recognition did ila sachani receive

solution_steps.explain: State the physical difficulty Ila faces from birth.
Trace how she turns her feet into tools of art step by step.
Say what her success tells about courage and determination.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does the molten brass take the shape of the figure in Dhokra craft?

solution_template.explain: The clay-covered figure is heated so the wax melts and flows out, leaving a hollow mould.
Liquid brass poured into the hollow sets in exactly the space the wax left behind.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What makes Bharat attractive to travellers, according to the passage?

solution_template.explain: Rivers, lakes, high mountains and green forests full of life are named.
People living in unison and a rich, diverse culture complete the attraction.
